content.value_statement: Astronomy workflows need reliable units, coordinates, time systems, and FITS handling. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Astropy patterns for scientific data analysis.
actual_capabilities: Guides Astropy unit conversion, quantities, equivalencies, and unit-aware calculations.
Explains celestial coordinate creation, frame transformations, separations, and catalog matching.
Supports FITS image and table workflows, including headers, HDUs, and large-file handling.
Helps build Astropy table operations for filtering, joins, grouping, stacking, and masked data.
Covers cosmology, time scales, WCS transformations, constants, visualization, and statistics.
limitations: Execution requires a Python environment with Astropy and related data files available.
Online catalog queries and downloads require network access and user permission.
Scientific validity depends on the chosen cosmology, units, frames, and source data quality.
Very large FITS files or catalogs may need local compute, storage, and memory planning.

use_cases.title: Reduce Observation Files
use_cases.description: Plan FITS inspection, header review, image statistics, and safe large-file access for telescope observations.

use_cases.title: Cross-Match Sky Catalogs
use_cases.description: Create coordinate-aware table workflows for matching, filtering, joining, and validating source catalogs.

use_cases.title: Teach Astrophysics Computation
use_cases.description: Explain units, cosmology calculations, time scales, and coordinate frames with practical Astropy examples.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Physical Units
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Astropy units to convert these values: [values]. Explain each conversion and note any required equivalencies.

prompt_templates.title: Transform Sky Coordinates
prompt_templates.prompt: Transform these coordinates from [source frame] to [target frame]. Include units, frame assumptions, and separation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a FITS Observation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the FITS workflow for [file name]. Identify HDUs, key headers, image statistics, and safe handling for large files.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Catalog Analysis Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Astropy workflow to cross-match [catalog A] and [catalog B], apply time or WCS context, and summarize validation checks.

output_examples.input: Convert 100 parsecs to kilometers and explain the result.
output_examples.output: The response states the converted distance, keeps units attached, and notes when scientific notation is appropriate.

output_examples.input: Summarize a FITS header and image statistics.
output: Identifies the relevant HDUs and important header fields.
Reports basic image shape, data type, mean, median, and data-quality checks.
Recommends context managers and memory mapping for safe large-file handling.

output_examples.input: Match two sky catalogs within one arcsecond.
output_examples.output: The response outlines coordinate creation, matching threshold, matched row counts, and frame consistency checks.

best_practices: Provide units, coordinate frames, time scales, file names, and relevant metadata in the prompt.
Ask for validation checks when converting coordinates, matching catalogs, or reading FITS headers.
Confirm the cosmology, data release, and scientific assumptions before using calculated results.
anti_patterns: Do not request analysis of unavailable local files without providing paths or representative metadata.
Do not omit units, frames, or time scales when asking for astronomical calculations.
Do not treat generated workflows as scientific validation without reviewing the source data and assumptions.

faq.question: Does this skill run Astropy itself?
faq.answer: It guides AI tools on Astropy usage. Code execution still depends on the local Python environment and user permissions.

faq.question: Can it handle FITS images and tables?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers FITS HDUs, headers, image arrays, table data, and large-file memory mapping patterns.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: Most guidance works offline. Named object queries, remote FITS files, and downloads require network access.

faq.question: Can it replace scientific review?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure Astropy workflows, but users must validate data quality and scientific assumptions.

faq.question: Which tools are supported?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide file names, units, coordinate frames, time scales, catalog columns, and the scientific goal.
